transcript: If we're being honest, I think Broadway has already kind of become a pit stop in the development of a new show. For the Wiz, the. It started as a national tour, and Broadway was just like one of those stops. It did a limited Broadway run and then it went back on tour, which is where it currently is right now. We have seen more and more shows continue their development as they went on tour and as they went out for licensing. Just because something is frozen on Broadway no longer means that it's done evolving. Just look at the evolution that musicals like Shrek and frozen took. And we talk about how shows rarely recoup on Broadway, but often times those shows can recoup on a national tour or in licensing later on. Of course, not every show should be on Broadway, and that was kind of what ended up being what the original commenter of the last video was trying to say, and I misread it. But even in that case, I do think that for some shows make going to Broadway just makes sense. And actually, if you end up getting nominated for a Tony Award, even for a very short running show, that is a huge advertising boost for when the licensing goes out for a show. And so even if a show flops on Broadway, having that signifier can be huge. And again, just the platform of Broadway itself is something that really benefits a lot of shows. Because Broadway is a space that rarely ever platforms black and trans artists. And so, yeah, I think that in that case, Broadway could be a really good Pit stop to platform, a really fantastic revival and then use that to fuel a off Broadway run where it could run for years in a really cool, immersive space. And so while I do think that there are shows that are able to thrive without ever going to Broadway, look at like every musical that was ever nominated as a revival under the classics rule, like Little Shop of horrors and assassins, or musicals like Heathers, which still have never gone to Broadway and like, are hugely popular. And most recently, we have the commercial run of teeth that is currently running at New World Stages and has never been to Broadway. And like I, I don't ever think it needs to go.
